solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Profit-seeker’s hat, the thing in front of a catalogue

indicators.note: being in front of something means coming before it, so one run of letters leads the next

blocks.note: a cap is a kind of hat
'it' is the pronoun for a thing
taken as written
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: An odd description of a money-maker's headwear, pinned to the front of a sales catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than making it possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invests money in business chiefly to make gains is the classic seeker after returns.

clue.text: Similar approach, not finishing Bible story

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short of the end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to come is to approach
a parable is a story with a moral, as told in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone never quite finishes telling a Bible story that takes a similar line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' is a verb here: COME loses its final letter to become COM.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can be set side by side and found alike are close in kind, which is what similar means.

clue.text: Disease often connected to small cow or chicken

definitions.text: Disease often connected to small cow or chicken

blocks.clueFragment: Disease often connected to small cow or chicken
blocks.note: surface reading: an illness passed on by little farm animals
setter's reading: the words 'small', 'cow' and 'chicken' each join the answer to name an illness

explanation.surface: An illness that farm animals, a cow or a chicken, supposedly spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the answer to each of 'small', 'cow' and 'chicken' and you get three named diseases: smallpox, cowpox, chickenpox.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a general name for infections that cause blistering rashes, and it ends those three illness names.

clue.text: Fair lottery excited mob a lot

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prize draw at a fair gets the crowd very worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tombola is a British fête game where tickets are drawn from a revolving drum for prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a raffle-style game of chance run at fairs and fêtes, where tickets win prizes.

clue.text: Minion’s facial bruise with the edges not visible

indicators.note: if the edges cannot be seen, the outermost letters at each end are dropped

blocks.note: a black eye is a bruise around the eye

explanation.surface: A henchman sports a shiner whose outline has faded.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Strip the first and last letters from BLACKEYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a servile follower who carries out a master's orders without question.

clue.text: Keep quiet on Socialist scrap

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing sitting on another sits above it, so the first part comes first

blocks.note: 'sh!' is the call to keep quiet
a Red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Someone is told to say nothing about a left-wing quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight to go with the politics, but it is a small torn piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny torn fragment of paper or cloth is a small leftover piece, the noun sense of scrap.

clue.text: UN regime reformed foundation for Pavlova

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A United Nations-imposed government reform lays the groundwork for a ballerina's career.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavlova looks like the ballerina Anna Pavlova, but it is the dessert named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavlova dessert is built on a crisp base of baked whisked egg white and sugar, topped with cream and fruit.

clue.text: Possibly a quotation of at the most one million

blocks.note: MAX is short for maximum, the most
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A price quote capped at a million, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quotation' suggests a price estimate, but here it is a quoted saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy saying expressing a general truth is often quoted, so it may be an example of a quotation.

clue.text: Work history, looking after patients coming to US casualty department

indicators.note: one thing coming to another arrives beside it, so the two parts are joined end to end

blocks.note: care is the looking after of patients
ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: A nurse's CV: caring for patients before moving to an American emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is the British name for a hospital's accident and emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: The course of someone's professional life across jobs over the years is their working story.

clue.text: Method of wiring limb in alternative therapy

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different form, so the letters take a different order
one thing sitting inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a leg is a limb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complementary medicine that involves wiring up a patient's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative therapy' reads as one phrase meaning complementary medicine, but 'alternative' is the anagram signal working on the second word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wire someone once meant to send a telegram, and sending messages by electric signals along cables was that system.

clue.text: Venomous creature like viper, at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

blocks.note: 'as' and 'like' both mean in the manner of
the middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A poisonous animal that is, deep down, a sort of viper.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma misleads: 'at heart' applies only to viper, not to the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a small poisonous snake of Egypt, famous for Cleopatra's death, so a venomous animal.

clue.text: Maybe mother’s personal assistant hiring fee

blocks.note: PA is the abbreviation for personal assistant
a rental is a charge paid to hire something

explanation.surface: A mum's PA charges her for being taken on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: a mother's things belong to a parent, as the question-free 'maybe' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a mother is one case of belonging to a father or mother, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Top Gear where carport is typically built?

blocks.note: first meaning: the highest gear of a vehicle's gearbox
second meaning, read as two words: a car shelter usually stands above the paved way up to a house

explanation.surface: A question from the British TV motoring show about where to put a car shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a long-running BBC motoring programme, which makes the capitals look like a title. Split the answer as OVER DRIVE for the second, whimsical meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra-high ratio above normal top in a car's gearbox is exactly the highest gear available.

clue.text: Way to follow sailor overseas

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the second part is placed behind the first

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Tracking a seaman as he heads off to foreign lands.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Way' first, but because it follows, the sailor comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being in or going to a foreign country across the sea.

clue.text: Switch between two positions, as leg got twisted

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters are put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shifts their stance back and forth after spraining a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' is a verb here, not a light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip a setting on and off, alternating between two states, is the verb sense used in computing.

clue.text: Supervise selection from Shinto verse epic

indicators.note: a selection is a portion taken out, so the letters run inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words once the spaces are ignored

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to direct a reading chosen from a long Japanese religious poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Shinto is the traditional religion of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct work or people is to manage it from above.

clue.text: Manage to secure short period in office when it’s cold

definitions.note: a time phrase standing for the noun naming that season

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: to win something is to manage to secure it
a term is a spell in office

explanation.surface: A politician scrapes a brief spell in office during the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' looks like a container signal, but 'manage to secure' is one phrase meaning obtain. TERM drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest of the four seasons is the time of year defined by low temperatures and frost.

clue.text: Touch down before team secures 50 for decisive win

indicators.note: coming before means placed in front, so the first part leads
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: an aircraft that touches down lands
a side is a team
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A rugby try followed by a team reaching fifty points seals an emphatic victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch down' suggests scoring in rugby, but it is an aircraft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming election victory by a huge margin is called this, after the sweeping fall of earth.

clue.text: Perhaps react with disgust, energy and animosity

blocks.note: spitting is one way to show disgust
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone responds in revulsion, with vigour and hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks an example: spitting is one possible reaction of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a malicious desire to hurt or annoy someone, ill will held toward them.

clue.text: Some of clever ruses go wrong

indicators.note: only some of the words are used, so the letters sit inside them

blocks.note: the letters bridge the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Not every cunning trick works out; some fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go wrong' looks like it describes the ruses, but it is the definition, and 'Some of' points inside the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a mistake or stray from what is correct is the old verb for blundering.

clue.text: Despicable person embracing Conservative is bigot

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a rat is a contemptible person
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the nasty type who hugs the Tories is prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link to the definition, but it goes inside the rat along with C.
explanation.definitionFit: A person prejudiced against others because of their ethnicity is one intolerant kind of narrow-minded person.

clue.text: Flake of hard skin almost touching soft skin on head

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
things touching sit right next to each other, so the parts join end to end

blocks.note: a scale is a flake of hardened skin
P, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A dry flake of skin nearly reaches the tender skin on someone's head, like dandruff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft skin' reads as a pair, but 'soft' alone gives P and 'skin on head' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin covering the top of the human head, where the hair grows, is exactly this.

clue.text: The man dismissed from Ashes is a fool

indicators.note: someone dismissed from a place is sent out of it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: 'he' is the pronoun for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer dropped from the Ashes squad is dismissed as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia; 'dismissed' sounds like a batsman given out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid or silly person is called by the name of the donkey, proverbially dim.

clue.text: Float around without hearing organs in brave style

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to fly is to float through the air
lacking ears means having none

explanation.surface: Someone drifts about, deaf to everything, with great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like an instruction to remove letters, but 'without hearing organs' simply describes having no ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with no fear, boldly and courageously, is doing things in a brave manner.
